classification.difficultyReason: Uses the identities supplied in part (a), converts the edge rate to centimetres per minute, obtains an edge length from volume and solves a quadratic rate equation.

content.prompt: The side length $x$ of a shrinking cube is decreasing at a constant rate of 5 mm per minute.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the rates of change of volume $V$, surface area $A$, and the total edge length $\ell$ are
$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=3x^2\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=12x\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)\\\frac{d\ell}{dt}&=12\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right).\end{aligned}$

spec.description: Oblique wireframe cube with a square front face, depth upwards and right, and three dashed concealed edges meeting at the rear lower-left vertex. No face shading.
spec.mathematics: All cube edges have length x. Three source labels identify the front bottom edge, lower-right depth edge and rear-right vertical edge.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and three x labels are permanent question content.

answer.short: $V=x^3$, $A=6x^2$, $\ell=12x$. Applying the chain rule gives the three stated identities.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which volume, surface area and edge length are decreasing when:

answer.short: Volume: $1350\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$; surface area: $180\text{ cm}^2/\text{min}$; total edge length: $6\text{ cm}/\text{min}$, all decreasing.
answer.worked:
$$\frac{dx}{dt}=-5\text{ mm}/\text{min}=-0.5\text{ cm}/\text{min}.$$
At $x=30$ cm:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=3(30)^2(-0.5)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-1350\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=12(30)(-0.5)\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=-180\text{ cm}^2/\text{min}\\\frac{d\ell}{dt}&=12(-0.5)\\\frac{d\ell}{dt}&=-6\text{ cm}/\text{min}\end{aligned}$$
The negative signs indicate decreases.

answer.short: Volume: $600\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$; surface area: $120\text{ cm}^2/\text{min}$; total edge length: $6\text{ cm}/\text{min}$, all decreasing.
answer.worked:
$$\frac{dx}{dt}=-0.5\text{ cm}/\text{min}.$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^3&=8000\\x&=20\text{ cm}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=3(20)^2(-0.5)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-600\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=12(20)(-0.5)\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=-120\text{ cm}^2/\text{min}\\\frac{d\ell}{dt}&=12(-0.5)\\\frac{d\ell}{dt}&=-6\text{ cm}/\text{min}\end{aligned}$$
The negative signs indicate decreases.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the side length when the volume is decreasing at $300\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$.

answer.worked:
$$\frac{dx}{dt}=-0.5\text{ cm}/\text{min},\qquad \frac{dV}{dt}=-300\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}.$$
$$\begin{aligned}-300&=3x^2(-0.5)\\-300&=-1.5x^2\\x^2&=200\\x&=10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
Take the positive root because $x$ is a length.
